messages:
incident_bot: ALERT: sudden RPM spike on cormorant9b across us-east-1 and eu-west-1. autoscaler at 98% and a few 429s reported. paging oncall now. :rotating_light:

alice: I see the alert, digging into metrics now. Is this affecting all clients or a subset?

ben: Prometheus shows sustained RPM up 4x for cormorant9b in the last 6m. Latency p95 creeping but not yet critical. Error rate (429/503) up ~2%.

carla: Runtime traces show KV cache pressure and some shard hotness on gpu-pool-3. Could be a traffic concentration to specific hosts.

alice: Quick customer impact check — @dinesh can you scan support for high-sev tickets tied to cormorant9b?

dinesh: Scanning... 3 active support threads mentioning timeouts, one enterprise (acct: AcmeCorp) with retries. Acme reported degraded chat experience.

alice: Ok. Plan: 1) soft throttle cormorant9b (lower RPM and TPM) 2) enable fallback to pelican14b-small for requests that allow model downgrade 3) temporarily disable function-calling on cormorant9b to reduce kernel pressure. Anyone object?

ben: +1. Recommend graceful ramp down: --tpm to 250, --rpm to 15000 initially. Watch for queued latency.

carla: Also toggle per-route routing to divert non-enterprise traffic preferentially to pelican14b-small. Keep Acme on cormorant9b if possible but at reduced rate.

alice: Executing mitigation now. CLI commands below. Posting for audit: 

```
# emergency sculpt: reduce per-model quotas
redwood admin quota set --model cormorant9b --tpm 250 --rpm 15000 --scope global --reason "emergency: rpm spike 3135800001"
redwood admin feature-toggles set --model cormorant9b --feature function_calling --enabled false --reason "reduce kernel pressure"
redwood routing set --from cormorant9b --to pelican14b-small --percent 40 --reason "deprioritize non-enterprise"
```

incident_bot: ACTION: quota change applied by alice. Change id qc_3135800001. feature toggle updated. routing rule pinned.

ben: Seeing immediate drop in RPM on cormorant9b down ~35% over 90s. pelican14b-small traffic +38%. Error rate stabilizing but p95 token latency up slightly on pelican.

dinesh: AcmeCorp still has degraded calls, but retries are lower. Raising a support priority to keep them informed.

carla: Checking backend: GPU pool utilization dropping on pool-3 but some hosts still hot. I'm going to trigger a soft redispatch to spread KV caches.

alice: Good. Next, we should carve out a small emergency spare capacity for enterprise customers. Proposal: whitelist AcmeCorp and two other enterprise accounts to keep their previous TPM but with a stricter per-minute burst cap. Something like: keep tpm at 800 for AcmeCorp but apply burst_window=60s limit 150. Thoughts?

ben: Agree. Implementing now via per-customer quota tweak. Command: 

```
redwood admin quota set --model cormorant9b --customer AcmeCorp --tpm 800 --rpm 48000 --burst 150 --reason "enterprise carveout during spike"
```

incident_bot: ACTION: per-customer quota applied qc_3135800001_acme.

dinesh: Notified Acme on the incident channel and explained temporary limits and fallback behavior. They responded :thumbsup: and asked for ETA.

alice: ETA: we'll monitor for 20-30m. If RPM remains elevated we'll either increase pelican capacity or pull more weight off cormorant9b.

carla: Also enabling additional logging for requests that hit fallback so we can detect quality regressions.

ben: Can we temporarily disable large-context jobs on cormorant9b? Those seem expensive and likely contributors.

alice: Yes — adding route rule to reject requests with max_tokens > 2048 on cormorant9b with soft-fallback to pelican14b-small. Command: 

```
redwood routing set --model cormorant9b --rule "if max_tokens>2048 then route pelican14b-small" --reason "limit long-context to reduce pressure"
```

incident_bot: NOTE: policy changes deployed. Audit id pol_3135800001.

ben: After changes, aggregate error rate back to baseline. RPM trending down to normal over 12m. p95 for cormorant9b improving.

carla: I'm still seeing 2 hosts with persistent KV spills — I'll reprovision them into replacement pool and drain. ETA 10m.

alice: Ok — I'll prepare a handoff to the next oncall in 30m with actions and outstanding items: 1) monitor qc_3135800001 and pol_3135800001 2) ensure drain completes and hosts replaced 3) validate no regression for enterprise fallbacks 4) decide whether to revert function-calling toggle.

dinesh: Support will keep Acme updated and close the loop after host drains.

alice: Handoff note: if RPM creeps back up, consider incremental tpm adjustments in 100/tpm steps and increase pelican routing in 15% increments. Escalate to infra if autoscaler is saturated again.

ben: Locking this thread and will check back in 30m for final status.

incident_bot: HANDOFF: oncall alice -> ben in 30m. Thread tagged incident: cormorant9b_rpm_spike.

ben: Acknowledged, taking post-handoff monitoring.

alice: Thanks team. Leaving notes in #incident-archives and will follow up with a short RCA if this recurs. :white_check_mark:
